unresolved.problem: Part 1 puts Westlands north-west and South B south-east. Part 2 gives w=(6;5), which is north-east, and s=(−4;−6), which is south-west, so the same two journeys have different directions. The Part 2 exemplar admits the mismatch ('do not match the compass words of Lesson 1 exactly') instead of fixing it. This also disagrees with Lesson 1, which fixes the directions as north-west and south-east. The coordinates should be changed to something like w≈(−6;5) and s≈(5;−6), or the compass words changed.

The claim that w=(6;5) and s=(−4;−6) 'point in opposite directions' is loose: the vectors are not parallel. The Part 5 exemplar then says even the magnitudes cannot separate the journeys, which weakens the premise that both matatus travel 8 km. The data (7.8 km and 7.2 km) does not support the 'same distance' wording used in the driving question and Part 1.
